newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria and Cameroon troops clash in Bakassi.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria and Cameroon troops clash in Bakassi.

text.p: Nigerian and Cameroonian troops fought briefly in the disputed Bakassi peninsula last weekend, local newspapers reported on Wednesday.
They said there were no casualties on either side and the fighting took place at night in Nigerian villages occupied by Cameroonian gendarmes.
There was no immediate confirmation of the reports from Nigerian military authorities.
Since 1994, the two African nations have clashed sporadically on Bakassi, which is believed to have significant oil reserves.
Troops of both countries are entrenched in the impoverished area whose inhabitants are mainly fishermen and speak Efik, the language of southeastern Nigeria.
Cameroon took its case to the World Court in 1994 but the court's ruling in March last year forbidding further fighting did not prevent clashes a month later.
